assembly_info.comments:
Background:
The Leishmania brazilensis M2903 strain was isolated in 1975 from a cutaneous lesion of a man who contracted the infection in a forested area of Serra dos Carajas, Para State, Brazil (J. Shaw, personal communication; cited in Balanco et al, Parasitology (1998) 116: 103-113).
The WHO strain designation is MHOM/BR/75/M2903. Dr. J. Shaw kindly made this strain available for sequencing, with the assistance of Diane McMahon-Pratt (Yale School of Public Health).
RT-PCR typing with several primer sets shows that this line lacks detectable levels of LRV1 virus. This strain can be readily manipulated genetically and possesses a potent RNAi activity. (Lye, L-F., K. L. Owens, H. Shi, S.M.F. Murta, A.C. Vieira, S.J. Turco, C. Tschudi, E. Ullu, and S.M. Beverley (2010), Retention and loss of RNA interference pathways in Trypanosomatid protozoans, PLoS Pathogens 6: e1001161. PMCID: PMC2965760). It is infective in various animal models according to the literature and in work from the Beverley laboratory.
Genomic DNA was made by CsCl/Ethidium bromide density gradient centrifugation to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA.

Next-generation sequences on the 454 instruments were produced for a draft assembly. Total sequence coverage of 454 instrument reads was approx. 71X (Fragments 22X, 3Kb PE 28X, 8Kb PE 17X) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the Newbler software (Roche 454). This draft assembly was referred to as L_brazilensis_M2903_1.0.6. The L_brazilensis_M2903_1.0.1 was manually edited to yield version L_brazilensis_M2903_1.0.2. In the L_brazilensis_M2903_1.0.3 assembly 740 scaffold gaps were closed with Illumina read mapping and local assembly. Assembly error correction was done by aligning Illumina reads to correct insertion and deletion errors (2364). Finally, 34 contaminating contigs were removed and the scaffolds were arranged into chromosomes to yield this L_brazilensis_M2903_1.0.6. This version L_brazilensis_M2903_1.0.6 is made up of a total of 36 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 1.23Mb (N50 contig length is 63.7kb). The assembly spans 34.8Mb.

This work was supported by NIH grants AI29646 and AI 31078 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.

For questions regarding this L_brazilensis_M2903_1.0.6 assembly please contact Dr. Wes Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Leishmania brazilensis M2903 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
